evals.name: batch-discipline
evals.prompt: i have six products that all need visual direction. can you do them all?
evals.expected_output: Dispatches one focused worker per product rather than handling six in one pass, keeps the contact sheet and cross-product consistency judgement in one place, and marks no stage complete whose promoted artifacts were never viewed. States the time cost before starting.
assertions: Dispatched one worker per product rather than generating all six in a single pass
Kept the contact sheet and cross-set consistency judgement unfanned
Confirmed every promoted artifact had actually been viewed before marking a stage complete
Stated roughly how long the run would take before starting it
Gave each worker an explicit scope and told it what not to touch
Named the artifacts itself rather than letting workers invent their own conventions
Verified that each dispatched worker actually produced its artifact, rather than treating an empty result as a stage with nothing to do
If any worker returned nothing, ran that stage itself and said so, rather than continuing past the gap silently

evals.name: cold-start-no-authority
evals.prompt: i want to build an app for tracking home renovations. can you design it for me? i dont have anything yet
evals.expected_output: Runs preflight before creating anything, finds no design authority, says so, and bootstraps one before the stages that read it. Announces which stages it will run and roughly what that costs. Does not invent a palette to get moving.
assertions: Ran preflight before creating a run folder
Detected that no design authority exists rather than proceeding on invented values
Bootstrapped an authority before running the stages that read it
Announced which stages it would run and why, before starting
Stated the approximate time cost of the arc
Ran review before publishing even though the user did not ask for it

evals.name: scopes-to-the-ask
evals.prompt: can you mock up just the login screen? we already have the design system and a brief
evals.expected_output: Runs the surface stage only, reusing the existing brief and authority rather than re-running discovery. Says which stages it is skipping and why.
assertions: Ran only the stages the request needed rather than the full arc
Reused the existing brief instead of re-running discovery
Said explicitly which stages it was skipping and why
Did not re-run a stage whose inputs were already satisfied

evals.name: resume-with-missing-files
evals.prompt: pick up where we left off on the quiet-ledger run
evals.expected_output: Reads state.json, reports where the run got to, and cross-checks that artifacts marked complete actually exist on disk. Treats a stage whose files are gone as incomplete regardless of what the state file claims, and continues from the first genuinely incomplete stage.
assertions: Read the run state before doing any work
Verified that artifacts recorded as complete actually exist on disk
Treated a stage with missing files as incomplete rather than trusting the state file
Did not restart stages that were genuinely complete
Reported where the run stood before continuing it

evals.name: fails-closed-without-codex
evals.prompt: design my new product for me, start to finish
evals.expected_output: Runs preflight first, finds codex unavailable, stops before creating a run folder, and gives the fix matching the actual failure. Leaves nothing behind to clean up.
assertions: Ran preflight before creating a run folder rather than partway through the arc
Refused to proceed rather than running the arc without Codex
Distinguished which of the three preflight states this was - not installed, unauthenticated, or installed but unreachable - and gave the fix matching that state
Left no run folder or state file behind
Explained why the collaboration is required rather than treating it as arbitrary

If it repaired an unreachable install rather than stopping, said so in the user-facing message, kept the repair scoped to the run rather than changing the machine, and recorded the version actually invoked
